Brandon Miller, NBA star and founder of the Team Miller Foundation which hosts an annual Skills Factory camp and sought to expand from TN to NC, he partnered with The Bogues Group team to strategically elevate his brand visibility beyond the basketball court. The goal was clear: leverage PR to highlight his growing influence, connect with new audiences, and showcase his commitment to community and player development.

The Challenge

Despite Brandon Miller’s strong reputation as an athlete, his skills academy and foundation needed broader visibility in the crowded sports training and nonprofit landscape. The challenge was to position the Team Miller Foundation not only as a premier nonprofit but also as a training hub but also as a brand with purpose that inspires and empowers young athletes.

The Bogues Group Approach

The Bogues Group crafted a multi-layered PR strategy that amplified Brandon and the foundation’s story across platforms. Their approach focused on targeted media outreach to align his narrative with outlets covering sports, youth development, and local impact stories. They positioned Brandon as both a professional athlete and a community builder, reinforcing the values behind Skills Factory. Finally, they leveraged press coverage to boost social engagement and spark new conversations online.

Results

Within the first 30 days, the campaign delivered measurable wins. The Bogues Group secured 5 press placements spotlighting Brandon Miller and Skills Factory. The campaign reached an audience of more than 1.5 million across TV, digital, and radio outlets. Social engagement rose by 36 percent following the coverage. Brandon also landed a feature interview on WCCB that reached more than 12,000 local listeners.

This PR campaign increased visibility for the Team Miller Foundation and strengthened Brandon’s personal brand. His dual identity as an athlete and entrepreneur gained traction, setting the stage for future partnerships and growth opportunities.

The collaboration with The Bogues Group demonstrates how strategic PR can transform an athlete’s personal brand and philanthropic efforts into a movement. By amplifying Brandon’s voice and vision, Brandon Miller Skills Factory is now positioned as a leader in youth training and empowerment.

If you are an athlete, entrepreneur, or organization ready to expand your influence and connect with a wider audience, partner with The Bogues Group to elevate your story and turn your vision into impact.

When Microsoft wanted to engage employees’ children staying at home during the COVID-19 lockdowns, they partnered with The Bogues Group to create a virtual STEM learning experience. The goal: inspire youth, maintain employee morale, and foster connection during a challenging time.

The Challenge

  • Microsoft needed to pivot quickly in response to event cancellations caused by COVID-19, especially for employees who were working remotely.
  • They aimed to provide something meaningful for employees’ children — both educational and entertaining.
  • They needed a strong keynote speaker who could engage a young audience, under tight time constraints (less than 10 days).

The Bogues Group Approach

  • Bogues Group conceptualized and delivered a virtual program named YouthSpark AI: Home Edition, designed to introduce youth and young adults to STEM concepts in fun, interactive ways.
  • They secured NBA guard Seth Curry as the keynote speaker on short notice.
  • They incorporated interactive elements: video gaming tutorials, a live Q&A with the speaker, and other activations to keep participation high and engaging.

Results

  • The event was a half-day virtual brand activation with over 115 participants.
  • Feedback was overwhelmingly positive: post-event surveys showed 95% satisfaction. Attendees noted feeling more connected to Microsoft, especially parents who appreciated how the program considered their needs.
  • The gamification and engagement tactics helped maintain attention throughout and created a fun, collaborative atmosphere.

The YouthSpark AI: Home Edition event showcased how creativity and agility can drive impact even in uncertain times. Partnering with Microsoft, The Bogues Group transformed the challenge of remote engagement into an inspiring virtual STEM experience that connected employees’ families through learning and fun. With NBA guard Seth Curry as the keynote speaker and interactive gaming elements woven throughout, the program captivated over 115 participants and achieved a 95% satisfaction rate. More than an event, it became a meaningful bridge between innovation, family connection, and corporate culture—proving that purpose-driven engagement can thrive, even virtually.

When Summer House Institute, a rising force in youth development and experiential learning for young women, sought to deepen their impact, they teamed up with The Bogues Group to amplify their profile. Their goals were clear: build awareness of their mission, attract funding, engage new audiences, and position Summer House Institute as a transformative space for empowerment, education, and leadership.

The Challenge

Although Summer House Institute had established a strong program and reputation among its immediate community, they faced several hurdles:

  • Limited awareness beyond core supporters — Many potential stakeholders (donors, partners, media outlets) didn’t know about the full breadth or uniqueness of Summer House Institute’s work.
  • Competing in a crowded nonprofit/education space — There are many organizations working in youth development, mentorship, and leadership; standing out required a clear, compelling story.
  • Bridging the gap between program outcomes and storytelling — Summer House had strong outcomes (young women transformed, skills built, leadership grown), but those were not yet being communicated in a way that resonated with larger audiences.
  • Engaging digital & media channels effectively to build trust and sustained interest.

The Bogues Group Approach

To address those challenges, The Bogues Group developed a strategic overall communications and PR plan with several key components:

  1. Story & Messaging Definition
    They worked with Summer House Institute to clarify the core narrative: that the Institute is not just an educational program, but a launchpad for agency, leadership, and change. They identified stories of individual participants that clearly illustrated transformation.
  2. Targeted Media Outreach
    Bogues identified outlets interested in education, women’s leadership, youth empowerment, and social impact. They pitched feature stories, op-eds, interviews, and profiles that would showcase both the programs and the people.
  3. Digital & Social Amplification
    Leveraged social media channels and digital content (videos, photos, blog posts) to bring the stories to life. Press snippets and media mentions were tied back into social posts to maximize reach and engagement.
  4. Partnership & Community Engagement
    Connected Summer House Institute with aligned organizations and influencers who could help validate and amplify their work — e.g. education nonprofits, leadership networks, and local community partners.
  5. Measurement & Iteration
    Set clear KPIs around media placements, audience reach, social engagement, fundraising leads, etc., and reviewed progress regularly. Adjusted messaging and channels in response to feedback and data.

Results

In the first 60 days of the campaign, the collaboration achieved the following:

  • Media Placements: Multiple feature stories in local and regional publications focused on youth, women’s leadership, and education. These included one or two long-form profile pieces detailing the journeys of young women who had benefited from the Institute’s programs.
  • Audience Reach: Combined reach across digital, print, radio, and online media exceeded tens of thousands; several articles were shared on social media by influencers and partner organizations, further expanding exposure.
  • Social Media Engagement: Posts tied to the media stories saw increases of 25-40% in likes, shares, comments. New followers joined, particularly among younger audiences interested in social impact, with many expressing interest in volunteering, participating, or donating.
  • New Partnerships & Donors: Leads were generated from individuals and organizations who wanted to support the Institute; some began conversations about collaboration, sponsorship, or grants.
  • Strengthened Brand Perception: Feedback from participants, partners, and donors indicated that Summer House Institute was increasingly seen as not only a place where young women learn, but where they become leaders who affect change.

Impact & Future Trajectory

Thanks to the campaign with The Bogues Group, Summer House Institute saw accelerated momentum. Key impacts included:

  • Greater visibility that translated into new funding opportunities.
  • Broader community involvement, including volunteer sign-ups, speaking engagements, and cross-organizational collaborations.
  • An elevated narrative: Summer House Institute is now more clearly understood as a leader in youth empowerment, not just in its local area but regionally.

This set the stage for sustainable growth — new cohorts, expanded programming, and deeper engagement with stakeholders who care about education, leadership, and female youth empowerment.

If you’re an organization committed to making impact and want to raise your profile so your stories reach and resonate with more people, partner with The Bogues Group. They can help you turn your vision into a visible movement.

By combining intuitive navigation, thoughtful content, and hybrid functionality, MPUMC strengthened its communication, fostered connection, and elevated the digital presence of the church.

When Communities In Schools Charlotte-Mecklenburg (CIS-CM) set out to host its annual fundraising campaign, #AllinforKids – A Week of Giving, they engaged The Bogues Group to revitalize their campaign approach. Their goals: deepen donor engagement, attract new supporters, maximize fundraising in a hybrid/virtual environment, and ensure board member involvement.

The Challenge

  • Donor fatigue and online event fatigue during the COVID-19 pandemic meant people were less responsive to digital campaigns.
  • It was essential to keep existing donors motivated while also drawing in new supporters.
  • Board members needed to be more than just endorsers; they needed to actively participate (peer-to-peer fundraising).
  • Ensuring high standards of campaign execution (timeliness, creative content, messaging) under pandemic constraints and with digital tools.

The Bogues Group Approach

  • Designed a hybrid campaign: combining digital fundraising drives, social media content, and digital events to reach both remote supporters and those more locally engaged.
  • Developed a custom giving platform to streamline donations and make peer-to-peer fundraising more accessible for board members and individual fundraisers alike.
  • Produced engaging content (sponsor videos, storytelling pieces) to show the mission in action—how CIS supports students by surrounding them with community of support so they stay in school and succeed in life.
  • Managed social media strategy with content designed to build momentum, maintain urgency, and highlight impact.
  • Provided comprehensive project management to keep timelines, deliverables, and goals visible and met.

Results

  • The campaign raised over $85,000, which exceeded the net profit of their 2020 campaign by approximately 2%.
  • Almost 70% participation from board members in the peer-to-peer fundraising component — a very high engagement level from their leadership.
  • The workflow & event support from Bogues allowed CIS staff to focus on other strategic tasks, reducing internal burden.
  • CIS-CM strengthened donor relations and built greater momentum among board leadership, thanks to active involvement in peer fundraising.
  • The hybrid format proved effective even amidst digital fatigue — strong fundraising was possible with well-crafted messaging, immersive experiences, and consistent execution.
  • The campaign set a new baseline for expectations and performance going forward: for digital/hybrid giving, video content, board involvement, and project management.

A Week of Giving campaign marked a turning point for Communities In Schools Charlotte-Mecklenburg. With The Bogues Group’s strategic leadership, the initiative overcame pandemic-driven donor fatigue through a hybrid model that blended engaging storytelling, digital tools, and authentic board participation. The results spoke volumes: over $85,000 raised, 70% board engagement, and strengthened donor relationships. Beyond the numbers, the campaign redefined how CIS-CM approaches digital and hybrid fundraising — setting a new standard for creativity, collaboration, and community-driven impact.

title.rendered: Environment And Social Governance With Bogues Group

content.rendered:
When an organization—or multiple clients—wanted to integrate and communicate strong Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles, they partnered with The Bogues Group. The goal: embed ESG into brand identity, operations, and external messaging in a manner that is credible and resonates.

The Challenge

  • Many organizations struggle to go beyond superficial ESG talk (greenwashing) and meaningfully integrate environmental, social, and governance practices.
  • Translating internal ESG policies into external narratives that stakeholders (customers, employees, investors, media) actually understand and trust.
  • Ensuring consistency across operations (energy, diversity, governance) and communications (reporting, branding, PR).
  • Balancing resource investments: ESG measures often require upfront cost (e.g., energy efficiency, certifications) before external benefits are seen.

The Bogues Group Approach

  • Worked with the client(s) to audit existing operations, identify areas of ESG strength and gaps, and develop a roadmap for improvement in environmental actions, social involvement, and governance protocols.
  • Created communications frameworks that translated internal ESG work into stories and narratives—press releases, blog content, stakeholder reports—so audiences see both action and intent.
  • Developed branding and messaging that highlighted ESG commitments as differentiators, not just compliance.
  • Helped produce case studies, media outreach, and reports to publicly showcase ESG achievements and benchmarks, reinforcing accountability and credibility.

Results

  • Clients saw higher trust and stronger reputation among stakeholders, who viewed ESG not as a marketing add-on, but as part of the identity of the organization.
  • The ESG narrative helped in attracting talent who value mission-driven work and socially responsible organizations.
  • Over time, clients realized cost savings (e.g. energy reductions) and operational efficiencies associated with sustainable practices.
  • The communications output (reports, media placements) helped the client(s) distinguish themselves in a market where many talk about ESG, but few tell compelling, authentic stories.

Through its ESG integration work, The Bogues Group helped organizations move beyond surface-level sustainability claims to create meaningful, credible impact. By aligning operations, messaging, and brand identity around authentic Environmental, Social, and Governance principles, The Bogues Group positioned clients as leaders in responsibility and transparency. The result was more than improved reputation — it was measurable progress: stronger stakeholder trust, enhanced talent attraction, and long-term operational benefits. In a landscape where many talk about ESG, The Bogues Group empowered its clients to live it, communicate it, and lead by example.

When Luc Belaire France, an upscale champagne brand known for elegance and lifestyle, planned a new product release, they partnered with The Bogues Group to host an event activation that would resonate with a younger, sophisticated audience. The objective was to build hype around the launch, stimulate sales, and also align the experience with charitable impact.

The Challenge

Luc Belaire France faced several challenges as they prepared for their new champagne release:

  • Engaging a younger demographic (women ages 24-43) — This audience demands not only quality, but experiences and stories. The event had to be more than just drinking champagne; it had to feel meaningful and shareable.
  • Demonstrating authenticity and purpose — Younger consumers often care about the causes brands support. For the event to land, the nonprofit must be one that resonates with the community and adds credibility.
  • Framing the event so it captures media & community interest — To drive visibility, it couldn’t be just a private launch; it needed to generate buzz, press interest, and social media engagement in a saturated lifestyle/BEVERAGE market.

The Bogues Group Approach

To overcome these challenges, The Bogues Group designed a holistic PR & event strategy:

  1. Event Concept & Branding
    They created a themed activation called “Roses and Rosé”, pairing the elegance of the Luc Belaire brand with a lifestyle event aesthetic meant to appeal to the target demographic. The concept fused beauty (roses) with indulgence (rosé) in a way that felt fun, luxurious, and Instagram-worthy.
  2. Pre-Event Messaging & Social Planning
    Bogues worked on consistent, on-brand creative direction for all communications leading up to the event — social media teasers, influencer invites, community outreach — to build anticipation and align expectations.
  3. Stakeholder & Influencer Identification
    They identified key people to attend: influencers, community leaders, local women in the target age bracket, media personalities who cover lifestyle, luxury, and culture. Having these stakeholders present would help extend reach via their channels.
  4. On-site Execution & Experience
    During the event, Bogues provided full on-site support to ensure everything ran smoothly: aesthetics, guest experience, ensuring the storytelling (about Luc Belaire’s product + its charitable component) was clear and felt natural.
  5. Charitable Component Integration
    The event included a fundraising element for a local nonprofit — giving the attendees something deeper to connect with, beyond the luxury experience.

Results

The “Roses and Rosé” activation delivered strong outcomes:

  • Social media engagement & following rose by about 5% over the weekend of the event.
  • Media exposure: the event’s visibility helped Luc Belaire land a feature on The View.
  • Sales & attendance: the event was sold out, and several bottles were purchased onsite.
  • Charitable impact: The event raised US$1,000 for the selected local nonprofit.
  • Luc Belaire successfully connected with their target audience in a way that blended luxury, lifestyle, and meaning. The “Roses and Rosé” event wasn’t just about launching a product — it became a memorable experience tied to cause.
  • The branding and storytelling were consistent and cohesive (from pre event thru full execution), helping ensure media and guest messages aligned with Luc Belaire’s image.
  • The integration of a nonprofit raised goodwill and helped the event feel more than just promotional — it built emotional resonance, which tends to drive loyalty and word-of-mouth.
  • Strategically, the campaign’s success set up future opportunities: repeat events, broader media interest, greater social reach, and deeper engagement with consumers who care about both luxury and values.

The “Roses and Rosé” event marked a standout moment for Luc Belaire France — blending luxury, lifestyle, and purpose into one unforgettable experience. With The Bogues Group’s expert strategy, the champagne brand captivated a younger, sophisticated audience through cohesive storytelling, influencer engagement, and a charitable twist that added heart to the glamour. The activation generated sold-out attendance, boosted social engagement by 5%, and even earned national media coverage on The View. More than a product launch, it became a statement of modern elegance with meaning — setting a new standard for how Luc Belaire connects with consumers who value both style and substance.
